dropped.why: ferrofast.com ISO 8750, schrauben-lexikon.de ISO 8750/DIN 7343 (d 1..16: a=0.3,0.5,0.7,0.8,1,1.2,1.3,1.7,2,3,3,4,4.5,5; d1=1.1,1.62,2.15,...) and Fuller's DIN 7343 page (d1 min=nominal) give different numbers; they describe the old edition and are NOT mixed into the table (GB/T 879.4 page agrees with the current-edition table, not the old one.)

dropped.what: column b of shear strength (second value row)
dropped.why: only sizes <=12 listed; meaning of a/b (steel vs stainless) not confirmed in the fetched HTML; also dropped length list (+ matrix of commercial lengths) because only one source (fasteners.eu) shows it
single-table schema; ISO 8748 table (d 1.5..20: d1 max 1.71, 2.21, ... ; s 0.17...) is visible identically in ferrofast, boltsfastener, boltport(7344), fasteners.eu but not compiled here

checks: d1_max > d1_min >= d1 nominal-ish > d2_max for all rows (e.g. 6: 6.5 > 6.25 > 5.85)
d1_max, d1_min, d2_max, a, s, F_a all increase strictly with d
d1_max - d1_min about 0.05-0.25 (tolerance band grows with size)
a column agrees between all four independent clusters wherever listed
two single-cell disagreements resolved by majority: s(2.5)=0.21 (Fuller 0.2), d1_min(12)=12.4 (boltport 12.34)
shape_hint: Hollow cylindrical spring pin formed by coiling a steel strip about 2 turns (spiral section, 'Spirol'-type): outside diameter d1 before mounting, both ends chamfered/rounded (chamfer length a, end diameter d2), plain straight sides, no head. Draw as a rectangle of length l with chamfered ends; the end view shows a spiral of wall thickness s.

role_map.d2_max: max diameter of the chamfered end (rise) before mounting
role_map.a: approximate chamfer length at each end
role_map.F_a: minimum double shear load in kN, column 'a' of the table

notes: Standard-duty coiled spring pin ISO 8750:2007 values (current table with d1 'before mounting' max/min). Sizes 0.8..20. Pin length l is a separate series (not published). Row support = independent source clusters agreeing on every listed cell of the row (Fuller; fasteners.eu incl. its DIN 7343 page; boltport; boltsfastener lists only d1 1.5-12 and not F_a; globalfastener GB/T 879.4 page). Independence caveat: fasteners.eu, boltport and boltsfastener may share an upstream (the same typo c max=33 appears on all of fasteners.eu/boltport/ferrofast for the sibling clevis pin ISO 2340 table); if those three count as ONE source the support is Fuller + GB/T 879.4 + that group = 3 for every cell except s at d=2.5 (Fuller dissents -> 2: GB/T page and group). Do not mix with the old DIN 7343 or ISO 8750:1987 numbers. For the same site hint families (heavy duty ISO 8748 / DIN 7344) a separate table would be needed.

A Chinese-template (1 cluster; producer: globalfastener.com detail_878 GB/T 879.4 page (live) -- same dataset/typo-free except Fuller s(2.5)=0.2 vs gf 0.21
C fasten.it: fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_7343 (live; d1 nom, d2 max (before mounting), a approx, s; no d1 max/min, no shear) -- producer reported this page as login-gated/no table, live fetch returns the table
Y older-edition dataset (dissents, 1 clu: ferrofast.com iso-8750 (table identical to lexikon incl. oddities d1=3.24, d2=2.35) -- shows ferrofast does NOT share the fasteners.eu data on this standard

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched live (HTTP 200) 9 pages (fuller, gf GB/T 879.4, fasteners.eu x2, boltport, boltsfastener, ferrofast, lexikon, fasten.it DIN 7343). Matrix 17 rows x 6 columns (d1_max,d1_min,d2_max,a,s,F_a) x 9 pages. Agreement of record with strict clusters per column: d1_max A,B only (2) -> fail; d1_min A,B only (2) + Y dissent at 8 sizes + boltport typo -> fail; F_a A,B only (+Y/lexikon 'Abscherkraft' for d1..16, but variant 'a' meaning undefined) -> fail; d2_max A,B,C = 3 for 16 rows, but row 3.5: A,B say 3.4, fasten.it AND Y say 3.35 -> only 2 clusters on 3.4 -> row fails; a: A,B,C = 3 for all 17 rows (Y dissents at 11 sizes: 22 cell-conflicts); s: A(gf),B,C,Y agree on all rows (Fuller 0.2 at 2.5 is the lone dissent inside cluster A; B,C,Y,gf say 0.21 -> kept). Sanity: d1_max>d1_min>d2_max, a,s monotone, s/d~0.08-0.09.
problems: Strict reading collapses producer's 'Fuller + GB/T 879.4 + group = 3' to 2 clusters (Fuller and globalfastener are one Chinese-template cluster). Only fasten.it DIN 7343 rescues d2_max, a, s (3 clusters, zero slack); d1_max, d1_min, F_a stay at 2 clusters -> dropped.
d2_max at d=3.5 split 2 vs 2 (3.4: A,B; 3.35: fasten.it + lexikon/ferrofast) -> row 3.5 dropped (a and s of that row would have been fine).

Two incompatible number sets circulate under 'ISO 8750': current/2007-type set X (A,B,C) and older set Y (lexikon, ferrofast): Y differs in a at 11/14 sizes (e.g. d=6: 2 vs 1.5), in d2 at 11/14, in d1 at 8/14. Record follows X (3 clusters vs 1); keep the 'before mounting' wording and do not mix with Y/old DIN 7343.
fasten.it page is labelled DIN 7343 (04/1969) yet carries the X numbers (except d2 3.5) -> edition label mismatch; counted as a numeric corroborator only.

F_a is 'row a' of 'Minimum shear strength, double, kN' (rows a/b); no fetched page says what a vs b mean -> variant undefined, label '표 a열' is neutral/meaningless -> dropped even though A,B (+Y) agree numerically.

Semantics of kept columns: fasteners.eu legend gives 'a - taper', 's - wall thickness of the pin', 'd2 - diameter rise', 'd1 - pin diameter'; record labels 'chamfer length'/'chamfered-end diameter' go beyond the legend -> relabel with legend wording (a = taper, d2 = diameter rise, before mounting).
Producer's own s(2.5) and d1_min(12) 'typo' resolutions are right (0.21 and 12.4) but d1_min is dropped anyway.
Family mismatch: family covers ISO 8750 (standard) + ISO 8748 (heavy) + ISO 8751 (light) + DIN 7343/7344 + KS B 1345; record is ISO 8750 only (16 sizes 0.8..20 minus 3.5).

standard_full: ISO 8750:2007 (standard duty coiled spring-type straight pin; DIN 7343 successor)
